summary: Saerji specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held positions at Peking University, including associate professor (attested 2010–2016) and faculty member (attested 2026).
Sagar Uday More works in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned an MBBS and DNB at Niga Hospital and became a member of the Epigraphical Society of India in 2025.
Sai Susarla works in computational fields and Indology. He served as Dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Sai Venkatesh Balasubramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He earned a B.Tech (2007–2011) and Ph.D. (2014) from SASTRA and an MBA from Assam Don Bosco University (2012–2014), working at IBM India (2011–2012).

Said Reza Huseini specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University (MPhil 2014–2015), Leiden University (BA 2015–2024), and the University of Cambridge (MA 2021–2025).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib. He worked at SOAS, University of Jammu and Kashmir, Aligarh Muslim University, and Australian National University (1967–1986).
Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MPhil at Cardiff University (by 2014) under Max Deeg and Peter Harvey. As of 2026, he is a PhD researcher at Ghent University.

Sakunoshin Motoda was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Kenyon College (~1887–1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1893–1895), and Columbia University (~1895–1896), later serving at Rikkyo University (~1899–1923).
Sakutaro Fujioka was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and subsequently held an academic post there (~1902–1910).

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under numerous masters, including the 14th Dalai Lama. He founded the Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and served as abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakyong Mipham is a scholar and teacher of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Namdroling Monastery and Oxford under figures like Chögyam Trungpa and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and served on Naropa University's board until 2018.

Sallie B. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1973–1975) under Leon Hurvitz and was a Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1992–2016).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley (1979) and studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, later becoming Senior Lecturer Emerita at UC Berkeley.

Sally McAra is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under Christine Dureau and Karen Nero, and was appointed an Honorary Research Fellow there in 2019.

Sally Mellick Cutler specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford (by 1993) and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996–1997).

Salome Zajadacz-Hastenrath was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the Pädagogische Akademie Aachen (1951–1953), the University of Bonn (1956), and the University of Cologne (1956–1965), where she earned a PhD.

Salomon Lefmann was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Münster, Berlin (Ph.D. under Franz Bopp), and Paris, before spending his career at Heidelberg University as an associate and honorary professor (1866–1908).

Salomon Munk was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied in Berlin, Bonn, and Paris under scholars including Schlegel, Lassen, and Silvestre de Sacy. He catalogued manuscripts at the BnF and became Professor of Hebrew at Collège de France.

Salvador Bucca was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore. He taught at the National University of Tucumán, National University of Cuyo, and served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Buenos Aires (1955–1983).

Sam van Schaik specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Manchester (~1996–2000), studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and served at SOAS and as Head of the Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library.
